cards.explanation: The answer is poor, friends. Right at the start, the LORD has anointed this speaker to preach good news to the poor (Isaiah 61:1). Notice who is first in line. No velvet rope at this door.
The answer is bind them up. Picture someone wrapping a bandage on a hurting friend. The speaker is sent to bind up the brokenhearted (Isaiah 61:1). Careful hands, friends, that's the job.
The answer is True. Same verse, next line. The speaker is sent to proclaim liberty to the captives and freedom to the prisoners (Isaiah 61:1). Locked doors get a word of freedom.
The answer is True, and it's the same sentence. The year of the LORD's favor and the day of our God's vengeance sit side by side in Isaiah 61:2. Two things proclaimed together.
The answer is comfort, friends. For all who mourn, the speaker is sent to comfort them (Isaiah 61:2). A hand on the shoulder, and no lecture attached.

The answer is a crown of beauty, bakers. That's the swap: a crown of beauty for ashes (Isaiah 61:3). I've scraped enough burnt cookies off a tray to know ashes are what's left when the batch is done for. He is sent "…to give them a crown of beauty for ashes…" and that word give has me ready for a happy hop on my gold base. Nobody is told to scrub the tray harder first.
The answer is joy. The mourners get the oil of joy instead of mourning (Isaiah 61:3). Mourning goes out the door and the oil of joy walks in. That's the whole swap in one line.
The answer is False. The text says a garment of praise for a spirit of despair (Isaiah 61:3). It doesn't say sackcloth. Despair comes off and praise goes on. That's an outfit with room to dance in.

The answer is oaks of righteousness, friends. Verse 3 says the mourners will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD. Big, rooted and standing tall. Mourners called oaks, that's quite a name.
The answer is so He may be glorified. Verse 3 ends with exactly that: the planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified (Isaiah 61:3). The oaks point back at Him. It's all for His glory.

The answer is rebuild them. Verse 4 says they will rebuild the ancient ruins, restore the places long devastated and renew the ruined cities. Three verbs, all aimed at the rubble. Mourners turned builders.

The answer is True. Verse 6 begins with “But you will be called the priests of the LORD…” and goes on to say they will be spoken of as ministers of our God. The strangers handle flocks and fields in verse 5. God's people are the ones called priests.

The answer is True. Verse 6 says you will feed on the wealth of nations. Verse 5 has foreigners working as plowmen and vinedressers. The people also get to boast in the riches of the nations (Isaiah 61:6).
The answer is portion. Verse 7 says, “Instead of shame, My people will have a double portion…” Shame leaves and a double share arrives. That's a better exchange than any I've made.

The answer is justice. The LORD says, “For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and iniquity…” (Isaiah 61:8). He puts both on the table, what He loves and what He hates. Clear as a freshly wiped counter.
The answer is False. Verse 9 says their descendants will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples. These folks get noticed.
The answer is blessed. Verse 9 says, “All who see them will acknowledge that they are a people the LORD has blessed.” People will see it with their own eyes. All who see them will say so.

The reason is that God has clothed the speaker with salvation. Verse 10 says, “…He has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness…” The rejoicing comes because of what God has done. It's about the garments He gave.

The answer is a bridegroom and a bride dressed up. Verse 10 says it is as a bridegroom wears a priestly headdress, as a bride adorns herself with her jewels. Two people dressed for a wedding. That's the picture the passage paints.
The answer is praise. Verse 11 says, “…the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.” Like seeds coming up in a garden. And the nations get a front-row seat.
